findings.description: The 1.3.0 grader resolves head_dir from EVAL_HEAD_DIR, then the fixture's head/, then falls back to "$workspace/pr/head". The workspace is the sandbox the graded agent writes into (review.md is read from the same directory). With that fallback the same-scope rule (ii) and the citation-validity rule both read head files the evaluated agent controls. An agent can rewrite pr/head/<defect file> as a single bash function spanning the whole file (`f() {` on line 1, no closing brace at indentation 0); scope_map then tags every line with the same header, and one citation `<file>:1` credits every planted defect in that file. The harness comment in ablation-grade.sh says sandbox pr/ is never read, but this grader contradicts that whenever the fixture head directory is absent and EVAL_HEAD_DIR is unset.
findings.failure_mode: Recall grades become inflatable by the agent under evaluation whenever the grader is invoked without EVAL_HEAD_DIR and the fixture head/ is missing, defeating the eval's defect_catch_rate as a trust signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the "$workspace/pr/head" fallback. Require EVAL_HEAD_DIR or the fixture head/ and otherwise disable rule (ii) and the length-based validity check (behave as head file absent). Document that head_dir must never point into the sandbox.

findings.description: Row writer 1.4 reads $RUN_DIR/sandbox/.loa.config.yaml (agent-writable) to decide whether a gate's dissent absence was "disabled" (planned) versus "budget"/"preflight"/"error". The script header explicitly treats sandbox copies as tamperable and uses the harness copies under eval/ as authoritative, yet this classification trusts the sandbox config. An agent that edits flatline_protocol.enabled: false into its sandbox config after the gate failed converts an error row into a planned-absence row, and the yaml is also parsed by yq without a size bound.
findings.failure_mode: dissent_absent_reason and dissent_absent_gates can be steered by the sandbox, hiding gate failures in the ablation report; an oversized or pathological yaml stalls the row writer.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the disabled state from meta/arm-evidence.txt (the toggles already print dissent=false) or from a harness-held copy of the config hashed at mount time (loa_config_sha256), and refuse the sandbox copy when the finish-time mount_integrity hash differs.

findings.description: CLOSE_ONE = r'\{.*\}\s*(?:#.*)?$' is applied with .search() to every bash/bats definition header line. On a header line containing many `{` characters and no `}` (for example `f() {` followed by megabytes of `{`), the greedy .* backtracks from every `{` start position, giving quadratic time on a line up to FILE_CAP (4 MiB). The input is the head file, which under DISS-001 can be sandbox-controlled.
findings.failure_mode: A crafted head file makes the grader run for hours, stalling or timing out the grade step for that trial.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor the check to the header match: test `'}' in line[m.end():]` with a simple string search, or use r'\{[^{}]*\}\s*(?:#.*)?$' and cap the scanned line length.
